display_name: Frieda Parker Hall (Purdue source name: Frieda Parker Residence Hall)

sources.provider: Purdue University ArcGIS BuildingShapesZip4 FeatureServer, layer 0
sources.geometry: single exterior polygon ring; 42 unique vertices plus closure

transform.formula: X_project=(longitude+86.9137)*84810.60416539927; Y_project=(latitude-40.4274)*111040.0; X_local=X_project-(-499.7250061); Y_local=Y_project-97.475; Z up, meters
transform.kind: project approximate local geographic conversion; not a surveyed CRS
transform.alignment_uncertainty: The transformed GIS-envelope center is about 5.48 m west and 0.35 m north of the asset origin. The source does not provide positional accuracy, and the assigned master placement was retained unchanged. The full asset bound includes site paving/detail objects, so the structural-shell envelope is reported separately below.

r2_footprint_comparison.calculation: Shapely polygon/rectangle intersection using the documented approximate transform; source GeoJSON FID 409 ring; major shell bounds from the pre-R2 Blender inventory.
r2_footprint_comparison.outdoor_patio_slab: 391 m²; outside the building polygon and treated as nonstructural site paving.

changes: Removed Frieda_NorthWing_Upper after the raw FID 409 overlap showed 98.1% of its plan rectangle outside the GIS footprint; its unsupported facade window details were not regenerated.
Removed the opaque brick upper breezeway/bridge mass and rebuilt its perimeter as glazed curtainwall with bronze mullions and transoms, following the official architect photographs.
Added repeated, material-differentiated windows to previously blank north, south, and west-facing elevations, following the official oblique imagery and documented residential program.
Combined repeated details by material into four meshes, keeping the asset at 542 objects total rather than thousands of independent window-part objects.
uncertainties: No whole-building elevation or curtainwall shop drawings were found in the reviewed public sources. Exact side-window positions, bay spacing, floor levels, and mullion spacing are visual interpretations.

Purdue GIS geometry was served in EPSG:4326 but does not publish positional accuracy; the project frame is a local approximation, so the footprint comparison is an alignment check rather than a survey result. The retained shell still has modest edge differences; those were not forcibly clipped to an uncertain GIS outline.
The five side/top previews are Blender Workbench inspection renders rather than photorealistic outputs.
